subject: Re: Next steps - Private VPC networking requirements (FinPay)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@finpay.com>, Olivia Martinez <olivia@finpay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps - Private VPC networking requirements (FinPay)

Hi Daniel / Olivia -

Great to meet earlier - thanks for the time and the clarity on compliance constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Recap from call:
- FinPay preference: Private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC) due to regulatory controls and data isolation.
- Primary concerns: network isolation, auditability (flow logs, audit logs), and limited ingress from the public internet.
- Networking options discussed: PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) vs VPC Peering / Transit Gateway. Security team currently leans toward PrivateLink but wants to confirm technical feasibility.
- IP allowlists: security team needs to know egress/ingress CIDRs for allowlisting and any static egress IPs for webhook/callbacks.
- Cloud: FinPay runs primarily in AWS (us-east-1).

Open questions / asks from our side:
1) Can you share a simple network diagram showing the VPCs/subnets that need to talk to Redwood?
2) Do you have a preference for PrivateLink vs VPC peering? Any organizational constraints that would block peering (Transit GW policies, org-level restrictions)?
3) Are you expecting mutual TLS for service-to-service? Do you manage certs in ACM or a private PKI?
4) Any required IP ranges/ports we should include in the checklist (we typically need 443 outbound and ephemeral for egress; may need 443 inbound if you plan to reach our endpoint).

Next steps I propose:
- If you can share a network diagram (attachment) we'll have Sean (solutions engineering) and Dev review for exact CIDR/route requirements.
- I'm attaching our Redwood Private VPC checklist to make review quicker.
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical sync with your network/security team this week to walk through PrivateLink config and route table requirements.

Attachment: redwood_private_vpc_checklist.pdf (attached)

Thanks - I'll follow up once I have the diagram.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

---
Note: This email and attachments are internal sales communications.

From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Olivia Martinez <olivia@finpay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps - Private VPC networking requirements (FinPay)

Marissa -

Thanks for the recap. Attaching a first-pass network diagram (finpay_network_diagram_v1.pdf). A few clarifications from our side:

- Cloud: AWS only (us-east-1).
- Security: our policy prefers AWS PrivateLink over VPC peering for third-party services because dept-level controls prevent peering to vendor accounts without additional approvals.
- Certificates: we use ACM Private CA for internal services. Mutual TLS is used for some internal endpoints; we can support TLS client certs if Redwood supports mTLS on the endpoint.
- IP allowlist: we need a list of IP ranges that Redwood will use for outbound callbacks (webhooks). If PrivateLink is used, we expect to allow outbound traffic to the interface endpoint; however, security will still ask for static IPs for third-party callbacks (we may need a NAT/proxy).
- Audit/compliance: SOC2 requirements - we'll need to validate KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and access to request audit logs for the service calls.

Timeline: pilot target = mid-April.

Attached: finpay_network_diagram_v1.pdf (see VPC layout and proposed routing).

Let us know available times for a technical sync.

Thanks,
Daniel Kim
CTO, FinPay
daniel.kim@finpay.com

---
Attachment: finpay_network_diagram_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@finpay.com>, Olivia Martinez <olivia@finpay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps - Private VPC networking requirements (FinPay)

Thanks Daniel - got the diagram and that helps a lot. Quick responses inline and next steps: 

- PrivateLink: we fully support AWS PrivateLink (we publish an endpoint service in the Redwood account). That aligns well with your security preference - peering is optional but not required.
- mTLS/TLS: Redwood supports TLS on the endpoint and can negotiate mTLS for mutual authentication. We'll need to coordinate cert exchange (ACM or an uploaded client cert).
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys for data at rest in Private deployments; I'll include the security engineering contact to walk through KMS controls.
- IP allowlists: for callbacks, if you want static egress IPs we can provide an option (via reserved NAT IPs in our dedicated egress pool) - I'll have Dev confirm ranges and any requirements for webhooks.
- Audit logs & SOC2: we can provide the necessary audit exports and SOC2 artifacts under NDA/attestation - Sean can coordinate the specifics.

Proposed immediate next steps (short bullets):
1) Technical sync (30 min): Sean + Dev + your network/security folks - propose Wed 2026-03-04 10:00 AM ET or Thu 2026-03-05 11:00 AM ET.
2) FinPay to confirm: preferred PrivateLink acceptance (yes/no), list of required CIDRs for allowlist, and whether you need static egress IPs for external callbacks.
3) Redwood to provide: draft network config (endpoint service name, required route table entries, security group example) and estimated IP ranges for egress.

I've attached the checklist again for quick reference. If Wed 10am ET works, I'll send an invite.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_private_vpc_checklist.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay prep - PrivateLink + allowlist prep (internal)

Sean/Dev -

Summarizing FinPay thread so you're prepped for the sync (Wed 10am ET):
- Account: FinPay (CTO Daniel Kim). They run in AWS us-east-1 and security prefers PrivateLink over peering.
- Key asks: PrivateLink endpoint service, support for mTLS (ACM Private CA), customer-managed KMS verification, and potential static egress IPs for callbacks.
- Attached by customer: finpay_network_diagram_v1.pdf - shows a single prod VPC with restricted outbound rules.

Can you each bring the following to the call:
- Sean: draft endpoint service configuration (svc name, required SGs, route table notes), list of required IAM permissions for acceptance. Also prepare notes on audit log export cadence for SOC2.
- Dev: please estimate egress IP ranges we can reserve for FinPay (small pool), and confirm support for mTLS and any performance implications if they enable mTLS. Also bring a rough token/throughput estimate for a pilot (50 reqs/sec baseline).

I'll send the invite once you confirm availability.

Thanks,
Marissa
